title: Astrid and the House
premise: Astrid Voss, who survived a childhood winter in her grandmother's house by never asking what lived behind the frost-ferned windows, returns as an adult when her nephew Casper—a teacher at a school where a class has vanished—sends her photographs in which every family picture now contains one extra chair. The house has begun collecting people, and it wants the debt Astrid's grandmother incurred to keep little Astrid alive through that long-ago freeze. Over one night, Astrid must uncover what was invited in before dawn, choose between offering herself or the truth of her survival, and finally break the bargain by naming the thing at the table and refusing its chair. She walks out at sunrise with Casper and the missing children, but the frost on the last window spells a new invitation.
about_author: Mara Joubert is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who grew up in a farmhouse where the windows frosted from the inside out. She writes horror about bargains, winters, and the families we assemble to survive both.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Astrid receives Casper's panicked letter and the photographs: fifteen years of family pictures, each now showing a high-backed chair no one owns, positioned closer each year. She drives back to the house she swore off, telling herself it's a prank. Emotional beat: dread disguised as denial—the past she buried is developing like film.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. At Hollow Creek School, Casper's homeroom is down to four students; parents speak of children 'staying with relatives' who have no relatives. He finds his own childhood photos bear the chair too—he was born in grandma's house. Emotional beat: isolation curdling into complicity; he realizes he's been explaining away the noises his whole life.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept Warm
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. In the sealed attic, Astrid finds her grandmother's ledger: dates, names, portions of firewood—and one entry from the great frost reading 'Astrid — paid.' The furnace room below breathes warm air though the chimney is cold. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of learning your survival was purchased with someone else's currency.

chapters.title: Roll Call
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper follows the absent students' addresses; all lead back to houses built by the same 19th-century builder as grandma's. In one basement he finds desks arranged in rows facing a wall of frost ferns, still warm. Emotional beat: horror of pattern recognition—the school isn't losing children; it's feeding them somewhere.

chapters.title: The Guest List
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Night falls early. Astrid's aunt Ilse arrives uninvited—or was she invited?—and sets a fifth place at dinner without noticing her hands doing it. The lights fail; the extra chair scrapes itself to the head of the table. Emotional beat: found family under siege—Ilse and Astrid cling to each other while the house tests who belongs.

chapters.title: Portions
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. Through the ledger and Ilse's half-memories, Astrid reconstructs the bargain: during the great frost, grandma fed the house a neighbor's child in exchange for warmth, then kept it fed for decades so it would never come collect Astrid. Grandma's death ended the payments. Emotional beat: grief weaponized—love revealed as cover for an unforgivable transaction.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper reaches the house with the four remaining students after their bus detours itself onto the property road. The door opens before they knock. Inside, the missing class sits at a long table, eyes frosted white, mouths moving in silent recitation. Emotional beat: protective fury—Casper stops being an explainer and becomes a rescuer.

chapters.title: The Chair Offered
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. The house manifests fully: walls breathing, frost writing names of everyone ever fed. It offers Astrid the chair—her seat, reserved since childhood—if she'll sit and keep the ledger going, warm forever, fed forever. Ilse begins walking toward it, entranced. Emotional beat: temptation at its most tender—the offer isn't terror but comfort, which makes it monstrous.

chapters.title: Naming What Was Invited
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid and Casper, alternating. Before sunrise, Astrid reads the first page of the ledger aloud—the original invitation, signed not by grandma but by the house's builder using grandma's desperate hand as witness. Speaking the name breaks the contract's silence clause. The frozen children wake; the chair splinters. Emotional beat: climax as act of witness—truth-telling as exorcism, identity reclaimed by refusing the role written for her.

chapters.title: Sunrise Pattern
chapters.summary: POV: Astrid. They walk out with nine children into thawing light; Casper and Astrid, uncle and aunt, become something like siblings in survival. But at the car, Astrid glances back: one window's frost ferns are arranging themselves into a new shape—an open door, and beyond it, a small chair. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—the price of survival is knowing it's never fully paid.
